raw_response:
I farm only 2 mu here in Quzhou, so I have to think carefully. Last year my wheat gave me maybe 450 kg per mu, and maize around 550 kg. Not bad. I will do mostly what I did before — changing things is risky when you only have 2 mu.

For **wheat**, I plant in October after the maize is out. I buy improved seed from the dealer in town — everyone around me uses Jimai or Shiluan type, they do well here. I use about 15 kg seed per mu. Before planting I plough once and spread compound fertilizer — one bag of 15-15-15 per mu, that is 50 kg. Then in spring when the wheat starts jointing I broadcast urea, about 20 kg per mu. My neighbor Old Wang uses a bit more but I cannot afford to waste. I water the wheat 3 times — once before winter so roots go deep, once at jointing in spring, once when the grain is filling. I have a well so water is not the big worry, but diesel costs money. I spray pesticide 2 times — once for aphids in spring, once when the head is forming to stop the scab disease.

For **summer maize**, right after wheat harvest in June I do not plough, just no-till and plant into the stubble — this saves labor and the ground keeps moisture. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu type, whatever the dealer has, about 2.5 kg per mu. I put one bag of compound fertilizer 15-15-15 at planting, 50 kg per mu. Then when the maize is at knee-height I topdress urea, maybe 25 kg per mu. Maize eats more nitrogen than wheat, I have seen this. I water 2 times if the rain does not come — at the big trumpet stage and when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide 2 times — once for the borer worm, once if armyworm comes.

My 2 mu is small. The whole fertilizer bill is maybe 600-700 yuan total for both crops. I cannot go cheaper because if yield drops I lose more than I save. Two of my sons work in the city and send money, so I keep farming mainly for our own grain and a little to sell.
